title: How to Track an International Payment in 2026: Status, UETR & Delays
summary: Learn how to track an international payment using a reference number, UETR or MT103. Check payment status and resolve delays.
body_markdown:
## **How Long Does an International Payment Take?**


There is no fixed timeline for every international payment. The time depends on the banks involved, currencies, payment route, cut-off times, weekends, public holidays, and any additional checks or documents required.


Some transfers arrive quickly, while others take several business days. Payments passing through[intermediary banks](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/what-are-intermediary-banks) or using less common currency routes may take longer.


If you're trying to determine whether your payment is late, check the following:


-


The estimated arrival date given by your bank or payment provider.


-


Whether the estimate starts when the payment is submitted or when it is released.


-


Weekends and public holidays in both countries.


-


Whether the expected arrival date has passed without a clear update.


If you receive money through a business[payment](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/global-payment-processing) platform, remember that collecting a payment and settling it into your bank account can be separate steps. Your client may have paid successfully even though the transfer to your account is still being processed.


## **Why is Your International Payment Delayed or Missing?**


A[delayed payment](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/international-payment-risks) does not automatically mean the money is lost. It may still be moving between banks, waiting for a review, or awaiting credit by the receiving bank.


Common reasons include:


-


**Incorrect recipient details:** An incorrect account number, name, or bank code can delay the transfer or cause it to be rejected or returned.


-


**Bank processing times:** One or more banks may need additional time to process the payment.


-


**Cut-off times and time zones:** A payment sent after a bank's daily cut-off may not be processed until the next business day.


-


**Weekends and public holidays:** Banks in the sending and receiving countries may follow different working calendars.


-


**Additional checks:** A bank or provider may need to review the payment or request supporting information.


-


**Currency conversion:** The transfer may need to go through currency conversion before the money can be credited.


-


**Intermediary banks:** Some transfers pass through additional banks, adding to the processing time.


-


**Receiving bank delays:** The money may have reached the receiving bank but still be waiting to be credited to your account.


The best way to narrow down the cause is to obtain the latest confirmed update from the bank or payment provider. If the payment is overdue or the status does not explain the delay, ask the provider to investigate.


## **How to Resolve a Delayed International Payment**


If the expected arrival date has passed, repeatedly checking the same status may not help. Use the payment details to find out where the transfer stands and which institution needs to take action.


### **1. Check the Latest Update**


Open the transaction and look for a new status, message, or request for information. If the payment still says "Processing" or "Pending", ask the provider whether it is progressing normally or needs attention.


### **2. Verify the Payment Details**


Compare the recipient's name, account details, bank information, amount, and currency with the original payment instructions.


If you notice a mistake, contact the sending bank immediately. Whether it can correct the details depends on how far the payment has progressed.


### **3. Ask the Sending Bank to Trace the Payment**


If the payment is overdue and there is no clear explanation, ask the sending bank or payment provider to investigate. Keep the following details ready:


-


Payment date or approximate date.


-


Amount and currency.


-


Sender and recipient details.


-


Transaction or bank reference number.


-


UETR, if available.


-


Payment confirmation or receipt.


Ask where the payment was last confirmed and whether it has reached the receiving institution.


The sending bank is usually the best place to start because it handled the original payment instruction and can request information through the relevant banking relationships or payment network.


### **4. Contact the Receiving Bank if the Payment Has Reached It**


If the sending bank confirms that the payment has reached the receiving bank, contact the receiving bank and ask it to check its incoming-payment records.


Provide the sender's name, amount, currency, payment date, and reference number. Ask whether the money has arrived, is waiting to be credited, or requires further information.


### **5. Keep a Record of the Enquiry**


Save the payment confirmation, reference numbers, messages, and investigation case number.


If the provider gives you a date for the next update, follow up if you haven't heard anything by then.


Avoid sending the money a second time just because the first transfer is delayed. First confirm whether the original payment was completed, rejected, or returned.


### **Can an International Payment Be Cancelled or Recalled?**


You can ask your bank to cancel or recall an international payment, but getting the money back is not guaranteed. It depends on the payment method, how far the transfer has progressed, and whether the recipient has already received the funds.


If you've sent a payment by mistake:


1.


Contact the sending bank or payment provider immediately.


2.


Share the payment reference and explain what happened.


3.


Ask whether the transfer can still be stopped or a recall request can be made.


4.


Check whether any fees apply and what happens next.


If the payment has already been processed or credited, the receiving bank or recipient may need to be involved. A recall request does not guarantee that the money will be returned.


If you suspect fraud, contact your bank or payment provider immediately and follow its reporting process.


## **How Can You Track an International Payment Received in India?**


If you're expecting money from another country into your Indian bank account, start by confirming that the sender has released the payment. Then check with your bank or payment provider to find out whether the money has arrived or is still being processed.


### **Step 1: Confirm That the Sender Released the Money**


Ask the sender for payment confirmation and the reference number. If the payment has only been scheduled, it may not have entered the transfer process yet.


### **Step 2: Check Your Bank or Payment Provider**


Look for the incoming transaction and check its date, amount, currency, and status. If you're using a payment platform, check whether it has received the money and whether settlement to your Indian bank account is still pending.


### **Step 3: Check Whether More Information Is Needed**


Depending on the payment and its purpose, your bank or provider may ask for supporting information or documents before crediting the money. Follow the instructions for your particular transaction because requirements can vary.


### **Step 4: Contact the Institution Handling the Payment**


If the sender's bank confirms that the transfer has reached the receiving institution, contact your receiving bank or payment provider.


Share the payment reference and ask whether the money has arrived or whether anything is preventing it from being credited.


If you receive international business or[freelance income](https://www.infinityapp.in/blog/increase-your-freelance-income-with-infinity-the-ultimate-freelance-payment-gateway-for-freelancers) , keep the payment confirmation, relevant invoice, and remittance documents together. This makes it easier to answer questions and follow up on a delayed payment.


### **How to Track an International Payment Without a Reference Number**


You can still ask your bank or payment provider to look for a payment without a formal tracking reference. It may take longer to identify the transaction, so provide as many accurate details as possible.


**Information to Provide**


**How It Helps**


Sender's name or business name


Helps identify who initiated the payment.


Recipient's name and account details


Helps confirm the intended beneficiary.


Payment date or approximate date


Narrows down the period to investigate.


Amount and currency


Helps distinguish the payment from other transactions.


Sending bank or payment provider


Identifies the institution that handled the transfer.


Payment confirmation or receipt


Shows that the payment was submitted.


Invoice number or payment purpose, if relevant


Helps match the transfer to a business transaction.


If you sent the money, contact the sending provider first. If you're waiting to receive it, ask the sender to confirm the payment details. Contact your receiving bank or provider if the funds should already have arrived. Never share your password, one-time passcode, or account login details when asking for help.


## **How Businesses and Freelancers Can Track International Payments**


When you receive payments from several clients or countries, keeping track of every transfer can become difficult. You might have multiple invoices due, payments in progress, and clients saying they've already paid.


A simple payment record helps you identify outstanding invoices and follow up on overdue payments.


For each payment, record:


-


**Client and invoice:** Who owes the money and which invoice it relates to.


-


**Amount and currency:** How much you expect to receive.


-


**Expected payment date:** When the client says the money should arrive.


-


**Payment reference and status:** Details you can use when following up.


-


**Date received:** When the money actually reaches your account.


-


**Supporting documents:** Payment confirmations, receipts, invoices, and relevant remittance documents.


A client's confirmation that they've paid is a useful starting point, but it does not establish that the money has reached your account. Match the payment records to the actual bank credit before marking an invoice as settled.


If a payment is overdue, contact the provider with the reference and ask which stage remains outstanding.


## **How to Track an International Payment in Infinity App**


If you receive international payments through[Infinity App](https://dashboard.infinityapp.in/auth/signup?pid=website_v2&af_xp=custom&shortlink=dicqy0p3&source_caller=ui&onelink_id=9OsN&af_dp=infinity%3A%2F%2F) , QuickLinks helps you check payment collection, while Transactions lets you follow processing and settlement. These are separate stages: a completed checkout does not automatically mean the money has reached your Indian bank account.


### **How to Track a Transaction in Infinity**


1.


Open Transactions in your Infinity account.


2.


Select All Transactions to see the full list, Processing for transactions still being handled, or Success for completed records.


3.


Use Filter, Clients, and Time period to narrow down the results.


4.


Check the date, client name, status, description, and amount.


5.


Open the transaction to view its details and timeline.


The timeline may show when the transfer was initiated, when the transfer to your INR account began, when it was completed, and when the FIRA was generated.


Can't find a transaction? Clear your filters and check the date and currency before contacting support.


### **How to Check a QuickLinks Payment**


If your client paid through an[Infinity QuickLink](https://www.infinityapp.in/quicklinks) :


1.


Open QuickLinks and find the relevant link or invoice.


2.


Check its status and confirm that the client, amount, and currency match your payment request.


3.


Once the payment is recorded, open the related transaction to follow its settlement.


If the client says they were charged but the link still shows a pending status, don't ask them to pay again straight away. A charge notification does not necessarily mean the payment has settled to your account.


If the payment remains unresolved, contact Infinity support atsupport@infinityapp.in . Share the link or invoice reference, payment time, amount, and currency. Include the transaction reference if available so the team can investigate the correct payment.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Tracking International Payments**


### **1. Can I track an international payment without a reference number?**


Yes. Contact the sending bank or payment provider, or the receiving institution if you're waiting for the money. Share the sender and recipient details, payment date, amount, currency, and any payment confirmation you have.


A reference number makes it easier to identify the transaction, but you can still ask the provider to look for it without one.


### **2. Can I track an international payment in real time?**


Not always. Some banks and payment providers offer live or near-real-time updates, while others show only a few processing stages. The level of detail depends on the payment route and the tracking systems used by the institutions involved.


### **3. How can I track an international payment sent from India?**


Open the bank or payment provider you used to send the money and check the transaction details. If the payment is overdue, contact the sending bank with the reference number and ask it to trace the transfer. Keep your payment confirmation handy in case the bank needs more information.


### **4. How do I know if the recipient has received my international payment?**


Check the latest status with the sending bank or provider, then confirm with the recipient or receiving bank if needed. A status such as "Sent" or "Completed" may refer to a particular stage of the transfer, so ask whether the funds have actually been credited to the recipient's account.


### **5. Can I track an international payment using a UETR?**


If the payment uses a relevant SWIFT payment message and a UETR is available, the reference can help participating financial institutions trace it. Share the UETR with your bank and ask it to check the payment.


A UETR does not guarantee access to a public tracking page, and it is not available for every international payment.


### **6. How can I track a payment received through a payment platform?**


Sign in to the platform and check the payment or transaction status. If the payment has been collected but has not reached your bank account, check the settlement status and contact the platform's support team if the expected timeline has passed.


### **7. What should I do if an international payment is marked as successful but hasn't reached my account?**


First, confirm what "successful" means for that particular provider. Ask the sending provider whether the payment has reached the receiving bank. If it has, contact your receiving bank with the payment reference, date, amount, and currency to check whether the funds are awaiting credit.
